title: Watching the numbers
purpose: One screen shows every phone, every hour, and every flag. Every problem has a name and a time limit next to it. We catch a bad day at noon, not at 8:00 PM.
how: Youssif builds the dashboard. The form feeds it. Mano chases gaps. Moharam acts on what it shows.

The device number and the wearer log join the phone feeds, so each phone is one row across the map, the verdicts, and the count, tied to the person who wore it. The evening check-out form adds what each site says about its own day. Alone, the map shows a phone online but not that it films the ceiling, and the count shows a site on target but not the flags coming.
Each alert goes to the lowest person who can fix it and moves up one level when time runs out. A known miss beats a surprise.

breaks.what: A phone shows as online but it has not uploaded anything
breaks.do: Online does not mean working. Trust the hours count. The operator visits in the same hour and checks the app is open, the wearer is on their own account, recording is running, and storage is free. If the phone is at fault, swap it for a spare.

breaks.what: A whole site goes dark at the same time
breaks.do: The fault is the line, the power, or the site, not the phones. The Portfolio Manager calls Moharam in the same hour, and the backlog alert above takes over.

breaks.what: A site is on target for hours but has many flags
breaks.do: Those hours are not accepted yet. The Portfolio Manager counts each flag as hours lost today and tells the worker within 24 hours. The invoice follows Youssef Medhat's verdicts, not the count.

The day does not stop. The company report page and the evening check-out form do not depend on the dashboard, so the 8:00 PM number comes from there, on time. If the form itself is down, each site messages its numbers to its Portfolio Manager, and Mano enters them the next morning. Youssif hears within the hour.

breaks.what: A site has not sent its evening check-out by 6:00 PM
breaks.do: The site counts as zero hours for that day until it resubmits the evening check-out form. At 6:15 PM the chase list of missing sites goes to Mano, who calls the site lead through the Portfolio Manager. A partner site with no report is not paid for that day. The number waits for no one.

questions.q: Why does the dark-phone alert go to the operator and not to me?
questions.a: Because the operator is standing next to the phone. You hear about it in the same hour. If the phone is still dark after the visit, it becomes your problem.

questions.q: The count says we hit target. Why is Moharam calling?
questions.a: The screen shows four things, not one. A site can be on target and still hold a device-day of backlog or a run of flags, and those hours are about to be lost. The call is about the loss the count cannot show.

questions.q: Why do we need 300 phones for 1,000 hours? A phone can record all day.
questions.a: Charging, restarts, dark hours, absences, and flags all eat hours. In real life, three phones give ten hours a day. Plan with that number and treat anything better as a bonus.

questions.q: A number on the dashboard is wrong. Who fixes it?
questions.a: The site that sent the number fixes it: resubmit the evening check-out form, and the latest row wins. Youssif owns the tool. Tell your Portfolio Manager the same day. A dashboard nobody trusts is a dashboard nobody reads.

feeds.name: MDM map
feeds.shows: Every phone is a dot: where it is, online or dark, last upload, and storage left.
feeds.answers: Where is every phone, and is it working?

feeds.name: QC verdicts
feeds.shows: Keep, flag, or delete for every session, totaled by site, phone, and wearer.
feeds.answers: Is the footage good, and who is making the bad footage?

feeds.name: Hours count
feeds.shows: The hours each site uploaded against its target, and the backlog in device-days.
feeds.answers: Are we on target today, and where is footage stuck?

feeds.name: Evening check-out form
feeds.shows: What every site submitted by 6:00 PM, direct and partner: phones out and uploaded, hours recorded and uploaded, wearers, phones down, flags, incidents, and gear needed. A site with no form is on the chase list.
feeds.answers: What did each site do today, and which site has not reported?

joins: Joined, the screen shows which site is losing hours, on which phones, who had them, and why: dark, stuck, or flagged.

alerts.then: The operator checks the app, account, recording, battery, and storage, then fixes or swaps the phone before the next cycle. The Portfolio Manager hears in the same hour.

alerts.trigger: Site backlog is more than one device-day
alerts.when: Same day, before the phones stop for the night
alerts.then: This is an incident. The Planning and Logistics Lead fixes the line, the router, or the hub. If the site cannot upload everything by end of shift, a hub run goes out the same day.
The Portfolio Manager tells the worker within 24 hours, with a specific fix. Three flags and the worker is off the project.
The phone stays paused until Youssef Medhat and the Portfolio Manager retrain the worker. Nobody can override it.
Moharam and every Portfolio Manager whose book is below target join. Each site below target leaves with a fix and the name of who will do it. The founders read the number with the plan.
